editorialNotes: No dollar figures are claimed on any slide by design; the brief notes the aquafaba ratio is the culinary standard.

copy.headline: Three of the best ingredients in your kitchen go down the drain every week.
Pasta water. The liquid in a can of chickpeas. Bacon fat.
items: All three go in the sink.

copy.headline: Pasta water. The starch and salt suspended in it are what bind sauce to noodles.
items: Reserve half a cup before you drain.
Add it to the pan a splash at a time.

copy.headline: Chickpea liquid is called aquafaba.
items: Three tablespoons replaces one egg white.
copy.body: Meringue, mousse, mayonnaise, all of it works.

copy.headline: Bacon fat.
items: Strain it through a coffee filter into a jar.
It keeps three months in the fridge.
It is cooking fat, and it is the reason restaurant potatoes taste like that.

copy.headline: You already paid for these. You have been throwing away the part that was free.
copy.ctaLine: Track what you have before it becomes something you pour out.
copy.citation: Save it before your fridge does the forgetting. Follow for more, something's on the way.
